notes: One object per recommendation, in benchmark order. page is the printed page number; pdfPage is the page index in the PDF file (printed page + 1).

level is L1 or L2 when the recommendation is in the plain Level 1 or Level 2 profile. BL means it is only in profiles that include BitLocker (BitLocker (BL), Level 1 (L1) + BitLocker (BL), Level 2 (L2) + BitLocker (BL)). profiles lists every profile exactly as printed.
expectedState is the quoted state from the title; comparison says how it applies (equals, notEquals, anyOf, includes, configured, configure).

registry lists the locations from the Audit section. expected is the parsed rule (kind: equals, anyOf, minimum, maximum, range, notEquals, blank, list, equalsText, anyText, unparsed); expectedText is the sentence as printed. A list policy (Chrome) is one entry for its key with valueName null, listValues true and the example values printed in the PDF (examples); valueNameInferred true means the PDF printed no colon before the value name and the last part of the path was taken as the value name, because a single value is expected.

valueType is the registry data type exactly as printed in the PDF. The values in expected carry that type: JSON numbers for REG_DWORD, JSON strings for REG_SZ and REG_MULTI_SZ (for example the string "0", not the number 0). typeNote explains an entry for which the PDF allows two types. typeConflict marks an entry where the PDF states a type that cannot hold its own expected value; likelyValueType then gives the type the value must have. microsoftDocumentation records, for such entries, what Microsoft's own documentation says about the type (valueType, summary, source, url, verifiedOn); where it differs from the PDF, Microsoft's documentation is the correct one.

description, rationale, impact, defaultValue, auditText, remediationText and additionalInformation are the sections as printed. Each paragraph or list item is one line (separated by a line feed); the line breaks inside a paragraph are joined. A line that ends with a letter or digit followed by a hyphen continues without a space (the hyphen is part of the word; the benchmark does not split words across lines). rationale explains why the setting matters for security; impact says what may stop working when it is applied.

references lists the numbered references, one per item, with wrapped URLs joined. cisControls lists the CIS Controls table: version (v8 or v7), id, title, description and implementationGroups. Implementation groups are cumulative, so the number of circles printed gives them: three circles = 1, 2, 3; two = 2, 3; one = 3; none (for example 0.0 Explicitly Not Mapped) = an empty list.
parserWarnings lists what the parser could not read for that recommendation. parserWarningCount in this header is the total.

registry entries with joinedFromWrappedLines = true come from registry locations that the PDF wraps over several lines. A line of 83 characters continues in the middle of a word (and a line that ends with a hyphen continues without a space); any other wrapped line was broken at a space.

verification records the independent checks that ran when the file was generated: appendix count, page numbers, every registry location and text field found in the PDF text of its recommendation, every expected-value rule rebuilt into the printed sentence, data types consistent with the values, complete Group Policy paths, no layout leftovers, every text section complete, no line-end hyphen that looks like a split word, and registry lines within the wrap width. The file is written only when all of them pass. The comparison with Audit.ps1 and Remediations.ps1 is printed when the file is generated but not stored, so this file depends on the PDF alone. textExtractor names the pdftotext used.

controls.title: Ensure 'Allow socket pool size randomization for proxies' is set to 'Enabled'
controls.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Edge\Allow socket pool size randomization for proxies
controls.description:
This policy setting controls whether Microsoft Edge randomizes socket pool sizes for proxy connections. Socket pool size randomization is a security mechanism that prevents attackers from using deterministic connection limits to infer cross-site information.
The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled.
Note: This policy affects the limits configured by the MaxConnectionsPerProxy and MaxConnectionsPerProxyForWebSocket policies. When enabled, the effective upper limit can be randomized up to 2x the values configured by those policies, though the expected increase is closer to 1.2x in practice.
controls.rationale: Without socket pool size randomization, the deterministic connection limit for proxy connections becomes a side channel that attackers can exploit to infer cross-site information. By observing when the browser stops opening new connections, an attacker can deduce the number of active connections to other sites through the same proxy, revealing browsing behavior across origins.
controls.defaultValue: Enabled. (Microsoft Edge enables socket pool size randomization for proxy connections by default.)
controls.impact: Proxy connections may use up to twice the number of connections specified by MaxConnectionsPerProxy and MaxConnectionsPerProxyForWebSocket. The effective connection ceiling is non-deterministic, which may complicate proxy capacity planning for environments with strict connection limits.

This policy setting configures "enhance the security state" in Microsoft Edge. Enhanced security in Microsoft Edge helps safeguard against memory-related vulnerabilities by disabling just-in-time (JIT) JavaScript compilation and enabling additional operating system protections for the browser. These protections include Hardware-enforced Stack Protection and Arbitrary Code Guard (ACG).
Enhanced security provides two levels of browsing security: Balanced and Strict. Balanced mode is an adaptive mode that builds on a user’s behavior on a particular device. Strict mode applies added security protections for all the sites a user visits. Users may report some challenges accomplishing their usual tasks when in strict mode. The recommended state for this setting is: Enabled: Balanced mode. Configuring this setting to Enabled: Strict mode also conforms to the benchmark.
controls.rationale: Balance mode will help reduce the risk of an attack by automatically applying stricter security settings on unfamiliar sites while adapting to browsing habits over time.
controls.defaultValue: Disabled.
controls.impact:
Users will no longer be able to bypass protection for previously visited unfamiliar sites. Edge will apply added security protections to sites that are not visited often or are unknown. Websites that are browsed frequently will be left out.
Note: Most sites will work as expected.
